top_story_title: No network device security news in this window
top_story_summary: Nothing in this collection window concerns network infrastructure. The sources returned a single fresh item inside the 24-hour window, and it is a mobile-handset vulnerability (an Android SMS-handling flaw) rather than an advisory or report affecting firewalls, VPN gateways, routers, switches, wireless controllers, load balancers, management platforms or SD-WAN edge devices. It was matched by the collector on a vendor keyword false positive and is dropped.
top_actions: No action required from this edition - nothing network-infrastructure related was reported.
Confirm your internet-facing VPN and firewall inventory still matches the vendor fixed-release tables you last checked, since no new advisories landed to prompt a change.
Verify management interfaces (HTTPS/SSH/API) on perimeter devices remain restricted to the management VLAN or out-of-band network.
executive_summary: No network device security news in this window: 709 raw items, 11 inside the 24-hour window, and the single item that passed the keyword filter is not about network infrastructure.
No new CISA KEV listings, vendor PSIRT advisories or exploitation reports affecting firewalls, VPN gateways, routers, switches, wireless, load balancers or SD-WAN edge devices.
One item dropped: an Android handset SMS-handling vulnerability with a public proof-of-concept, matched by a vendor keyword false positive and out of scope for this digest.
No vendor AI defence announcements in this cycle, and nothing genuinely AI-related for network gear - the AI section carries forward.
